battle.name: 隋衛文升平僚人叛亂
battle.brief: 仁壽元年（601），益州西山一帶僚人寨眾起兵反隋，州郡不能制，隋廷發郡兵與募兵往討。蜀道險遠，糧秣全賴劍閣道與岷江轉運。守寨一方據山梁高處以弩封隘，官軍亦以弩手壓制寨牆，再遣步卒緣梯登寨。戰爭列表記此役為『隋衛文升平僚人叛亂』，正史未載主將姓名與戰果數字。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 仁壽元年（601）益州用兵，參戰方大體分為兩個系統。一端是隋朝中央與益州諸郡縣的官軍：發兵與糧秣的權力握在京城，仁壽元年隋文帝楊堅仍在位，詔發郡兵、募兵往益州；益州總管、蜀王楊秀是隋廷在蜀地最高的軍政長官，州刺史、縣令與戍卒皆歸其節制。與官軍並肩作戰的，是已歸附的熟僚與當地漢人鄉兵，朝廷往往以「以夷制夷」的方式徵其為嚮導與先鋒。反方是益州西南山中的僚人（史籍亦作獠、俚）諸部聚落，並未建立政權名號，也沒有推舉共主，各寨自為首領，以山寨為堡壘，靠劫掠村邑、斷絕道路、拒絕官軍為務。官軍在兵員、器械、糧道與後方補給上佔優，叛方在地利、熟悉地形與前線耳目上佔優，這一攻守結構自始便定下本役的走向。嶺南方面同年亦有僚人起事，隋廷以廣州總管馮盎為行軍總管往討；兩地相隔千里，各州郡兵自守而互不相援，州郡武力之薄於此可見。
countriesEn: In the campaign of 601 in Yizhou the belligerents fell into two systems. On one side stood the Sui state and the government troops of the commanderies and counties of Yizhou: the power to send soldiers and grain remained in the capital, where Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, was still reigning in the first year of Renshou, and he ordered commandery troops and recruited soldiers dispatched to Yizhou. The highest civil and military authority in the region was Yang Xiu, Prince of Shu, Superintendent of Yizhou, under whom the prefects, the county magistrates and the garrison soldiers were governed. Fighting alongside the government troops were the already submitted settled Liao and the local Han militia, whom the court repeatedly employed as guides and as vanguard, the old formula of using the barbarians to control the barbarians. On the other side were the settlements of the Liao peoples (also written liao and li in the records) in the mountains southwest of Yizhou. They had set up no state name and no common sovereign; each stockade had its own leader, each made its stronghold a castle, and they lived by raiding villages, cutting the roads and refusing the government troops. The government side was superior in numbers, equipment, supply lines and rear-area support; the insurgents were superior in terrain, in knowledge of the country and in their information on the frontier. That balance of attack and defence settled the course of the fighting from the start. In Lingnan the same year also saw the Liao rise, and the court sent Feng Ang, Superintendent of Guangzhou, to deal with it as commander-in-chief; the two theatres lay a thousand li apart, each district guarded by its own local militia and neither able to help the other, which shows how thin the military strength of the prefectures and counties had become.
people: 本役可確定的關鍵人物，多數在史籍中只有身分而無姓名。隋文帝楊堅自開皇元年受禪至仁壽元年崩，十三年來每一次南方用兵都由他下詔、定方略、命將；他晚年多病，京城謠言紛起，遠近傳聞隋祚將盡，山中寨落把這類說法視為可乘之機。蜀王楊秀是文帝之子，出總益州，是隋廷在蜀地軍政的代理人；開皇末年他奉召入朝而不得見，益州人心惶惶，其後他被幽於京師，蜀地對朝廷的疑慮隨之加深，這是本役背景中最可指名的政治轉折。反方各寨首領的姓名多不見於傳記，只能確定有一批俚獠首領趁隋廷在西南調兵之際舉事，眾至以萬計。同年嶺南之役中，隋廷倚重高涼冼氏所率俚族兵眾與其孫陳魂的嚮導，此例說明當時西南平叛高度依賴「以夷制夷」；蜀地之役是否同樣倚重熟僚，正史未明載。戰爭列表所記「衛文升平」一名，其具體所指（將名抑或年號別稱）亦無從對證；史籍記本役甚略，未載主將姓名、兵員編制與戰果數字，這正是此役在戰爭列表中留下名目、卻在正史中只剩一行的原因。
peopleEn: The key figures of this campaign are known mostly by position rather than by name. Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, reigned from his accession in the first year of Kaihuang until his death in the first year of Renshou, and for thirteen years every southern war was ordered, planned and staffed by him; in his later years he was often ill, rumours ran through the capital, and it was said far and wide that the Sui would soon fall, and the strongholds in the mountains read such talk as their chance. Yang Xiu, Prince of Shu, a son of the emperor who held the highest civil and military authority in Yizhou as Superintendent of Yizhou, is the one political turning point in the background that can be named: at the end of the Kaihuang era he was summoned to the capital and not received, which threw the people of Yizhou into confusion, and he was later confined in the capital, deepening the mistrust of the court in the region. The names of the leaders on the insurgent side hardly appear in the historical records; all that can be established is that a group of Li and Liao chieftains rose while the court was shifting troops in the southwest, and that the numbers involved ran to tens of thousands. In the Lingnan campaign of the same year the court leaned on the Liang forces of the lady Xian of Gaoliang and on the guidance of her grandson Chen Hun, which shows how heavily suppression in the southwest depended on using barbarians against barbarians; whether the Yizhou campaign relied in the same way on the settled Liao is not stated in the official histories. The name given in the list of wars, Wei Wenshengping, cannot be matched to anything certain, whether a general's name or a variant era title; the annals describe the campaign very briefly and give neither the name of the commander, nor the order of battle, nor the figures of the results, and that is exactly why it left a name in the list of wars and only a single line in the histories.
kits: 卡面那件秦弩，是漢代以來中國軍隊守城用的標誌性器械：弩機把弦的拉力儲存起來，扣機一放，箭矢直出，射速雖不及拉弓，射程卻遠得多。守城一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外，開皇末至仁壽元年益州一帶的寨城與州郡城，正是靠壘後與城頭的弩手維持封鎖。弩的極限同樣明顯：上弦費力，須藉器具輔助而非僅憑臂力，一兵不能連珠快射，一名弩手每分鐘只能射出數發，遠不及弓手的十餘發；弩機為木金機括，蜀地多雨多濕，弦與機括受潮即發力不順，故弩兵在雨季與連日陰天作戰能力明顯下降。隋軍攻城一面以弩手在盾車後齊射，掩護雲梯兵攀緣寨牆，一面用投石機與撞車毀寨門及守兵密集處；破寨之後的搜索追捕，仍靠步卒持長矛與環首刀近身格鬥。供養方面，蜀道狹窄，牛車與馱馬只能單列通行，糧秣自京師或劍閣沿涪江、岷江轉運，弩兵所需的大量箭矢則多由州縣就地備辦，遠程運來並不現實。
kitsEn: The weapon on the face of the card, the Qin crossbow, was the standard defensive arm of Chinese armies from the Han dynasty onward: the trigger mechanism stores the tension of the string, and when the catch is released the bolt flies straight; its rate of fire is below that of the bow, but its range is far greater. The defending side uses it to hold the attackers down outside the wall, and the stockades and prefectural cities of the Yizhou area in the late Kaihuang and first Renshou years were held shut by crossbowmen posted behind the ramparts and along the wall heads. The limits of the weapon are just as clear: the string is hard to cock and must be assisted by an implement rather than by arm strength alone, a soldier cannot loose bolt after bolt in rapid succession, and a crossbowman manages only a few shots a minute, far below the dozen or more of an archer. The mechanism is of wood and metal, and the damp of the rainy Sichuan country makes both the string and the mechanism work badly when wet, so the fighting value of the crossbow troops falls markedly in the rainy season and on long stretches of overcast days. When the Sui army assaulted a stockade it used crossbowmen firing in volleys from behind the shields to cover the men on the scaling ladders, and used stone-throwers and battering rams against the gate and the crowded places on the wall; the work of clearing the stockade and pursuing the fugitives was still done by infantry with long spears and ring-pommel swords at close quarters. As for supply, the narrow roads of Shu allowed only single-file ox carts and pack animals; grain and millet came from the capital or from Jianmen down the Fu and Min rivers, while the great quantity of bolts needed by the crossbowmen was prepared locally by the prefectures and counties, for bringing it from far away was hardly practical.
tactics: 隋朝在西南平叛的常規步驟，大致可分四層。第一層是固守城池與隘口：州郡城與寨城先以弩手、礟石封住牆頭，滾木與撞車堵住門道，使叛眾不能貼牆、不能架梯，也不許閒人出入。第二層是設圍斷糧：官軍不作四面強攻，而是分據山口與水源，斷絕山寨與山下村邑間的往來，山中缺鹽缺米，守寨者自潰。第三層是招撫分化：對願降首領授以官爵、仍舊牧其眾，把生僚與熟僚分開安置，同時以熟僚為嚮導潛行谿谷，避開正路直取寨後。第四層才是強攻：投石機列於後方高處，打擊寨牆、寨門上方守兵密集處與村寨屋頂，撞車撞開寨門，雲梯兵趁缺口攀緣，弩手在前列齊射掩護登城，步卒隨之湧入。叛方的戰法相反：依山阻險，寨築於崖壁或山梁，弓弩居高扼隘，襲擊糧道與後方輜重，並在谿谷中設障阻騎，屢以小股遊騎擾亂官軍側翼，使隋軍的圍圈與糧道始終拉得太長。官軍真正害怕的不是寨牆，而是蜀道與糧秣：一旦雨季延長或後方接應不繼，圍軍必先於守軍耗盡。
tacticsEn: The routine by which the Sui put down revolts in the southwest ran in four layers. The first was to hold the cities and the passes: the prefectural and county cities and the stockades sealed the wall heads with crossbowmen and stone missiles, while rolling logs and rams blocked the gateways so that the insurgents could neither press against the wall nor set up their ladders, and no unauthorised men were allowed in or out. The second was to encircle and cut the supplies: the government army did not attack on all four sides, but took up positions at the passes and on the water sources and severed the links between the stockade and the villages below, so that for want of salt and rice the defenders would break up of themselves. The third was to make terms and divide the enemy: leaders who were willing to surrender were granted official rank and left to rule their own people, the raw Liao and the settled Liao were settled apart, and settled Liao were used as guides to move by stealth through the ravines, avoiding the main road and striking the rear of the stockade. The fourth was the assault itself: stone-throwers were set up on high ground at the rear to strike the stockade walls, the places above the gate where the defenders crowded and the roofs of the villages; rams knocked the gate open, ladder troops climbed through the breach, crossbowmen in the front line fired in volleys to cover the ascent, and infantry poured in behind them. The insurgents fought the other way round: they held the heights, built their stockades on cliffs and ridges, used bows and crossbows from above to hold the passes, raided the supply line and the baggage in the rear, set obstructions in the gullies to check riders, and came down in small parties to harry the flanks of the government army, so that its ring of investment and its supply line always had to be stretched too far. What the government army truly feared was not the wall of the stockade but the roads and grain of Shu: once the rainy season ran long or the support from the rear failed, the besiegers were exhausted before the defenders were.
data: 可以確定的數字不多，逐一標明其確定程度。時間：起事與平定都在仁壽元年（601）之內，隋文帝崩於同年十一月，其後改元大業，故此役是隋朝以開皇年號平定西南的最後一批戰事之一；起事確月無可確證，本篇置於三月，屬依「春後用兵、糧秣未乏」常例所作的推想。規模：正史記益州俚族首領趙雙起事時眾達「十餘萬」，這是史籍對蜀地僚亂唯一留下的概括數字，可見起事方並非數百人的小股，而以數萬計的部落聯盟為後盾；同一史籍對歷次平亂只作數語，並無編制、斬獲、俘虜與器械損耗的數字。距離：成都至雅州約二百餘里，至邛州約一百五十里，蜀道狹窄，牛車與馱馬單列通行，偏師深入數百里後，糧秣全賴後方接力，極易斷援。器械：弩的有效射程一般在一百五十步上下，遠超弓矢，守城居高臨下再添數十步，一名弩手足以封住一段牆頭；但弩手每分鐘只能射數發，千人守軍配弩數百張，也只夠覆蓋一段城垣，故弩兵比例與城段長度的配算是平叛前的實際難題。氣候：蜀地多雨，秋季多陰雨，弦與機括受潮是雨季作戰的真實限制。
dataEn: Few figures can be fixed, and each has to be marked with its degree of certainty. Timing: the rising and its suppression both fall inside the first year of Renshou (601); the Emperor Wen of Sui died in the eleventh month of that year and the era name changed to Daye after it, so this campaign belongs to the last group of south-western wars the Sui fought under the Kaihuang era name. The exact month of the rising cannot be established; this account places it in the third month, an inference drawn from the custom of campaigning after the spring ploughing season, when grain is not yet scarce. Scale: the official histories record that when the Yizhou chieftain Zhao Shuang rose he gathered more than a hundred thousand men; this is the only summary figure the annals leave for the Liao revolts in Shu, and it shows that the insurgents were not a few hundred men but a tribal league numbering tens of thousands. The same histories describe the successive suppressions in a few words and give no figures for the order of battle, for the killed and captured, or for the loss of equipment. Distances: Chengdu is about two hundred and some li from Yazhou and about a hundred and fifty from Qiongzhou; the roads of Shu are narrow enough that ox carts and pack animals could pass only in single file, so a detached force that pushed several hundred li deep depended entirely on relay supply and was extremely easy to cut off. Equipment: the effective range of the crossbow is around a hundred and fifty paces, well beyond that of the bow, and a defender on high ground adds several dozen paces more, so a single crossbowman could seal a stretch of wall; but as a crossbowman looses only a few bolts a minute, a garrison of a thousand men with several hundred crossbows would cover a stretch of rampart and no more, which made the ratio of crossbow troops to the length of wall a real problem to be reckoned before the assault began. Climate: Sichuan is rainy, with long stretches of overcast autumn weather, and damp strings and mechanisms are a genuine limitation on fighting in the wet season.
cause: 起事並非單一事件爆發，而是隋朝在西南的體制與山地社會長期摩擦的結果。開皇九年（589）隋平陳後，益州全境歸入新朝，朝廷在山區新置州縣、編定戶口、徵發丁役、徵收鹽鐵與馬匹，並逐步削弱部落首領的傳統權力；州郡官員為求政績與私利，往往加派徭役、沒收山寨所藏兵器，豪酋則利用熟悉山道村落的便利截留政令，兩面互相告訐，積怨於谿谷。開皇末年的政治震動更提供了時機：蜀王楊秀奉召入朝而不得見，益州人心惶惶，其後楊秀被幽於京師，傳言隋廷將盡收蜀兵收歸中央，山中寨落遂把朝廷的內部動盪讀作可乘之機；同時隋文帝晚年多病、京城謠言四起，山地與嶺南的起事者都相信隋祚將盡。外部壓力也起了作用：陳朝覆亡十餘年，陳氏舊臣與遺民散入西南山區，以拒官軍、護山寨相號召，誘使各寨響應。加上開皇年間益州僚亂本身已數度爆發、每次都被壓下，兵員與器械的消耗逐次累積，郡兵疲敝，於是仁壽元年再舉時，州郡已難以自行抵擋，朝廷不得不發兵入蜀。
causeEn: The rising was not a single sudden event but the accumulated friction between the Sui system in the southwest and the mountain societies. After the conquest of Chen in 589 the whole of Yizhou came under the new dynasty; the court set up prefectures and counties in the mountains, registered the households, called up labour and military service, and took salt, iron and horses, while gradually reducing the traditional authority of the tribal chiefs. Prefects and county officials, in pursuit of their own credit and profit, added levies and confiscated the weapons kept in the stockades; the local magnates, taking advantage of their knowledge of the mountain paths and villages, withheld the orders of the court; the two sides denounced each other, and the grievance settled in the ravines. The political shock at the end of the Kaihuang era supplied the occasion: Yang Xiu, Prince of Shu, was summoned to the capital and not received, the people of Yizhou were thrown into confusion, and he was later confined in the capital, so the rumour that the court would strip the troops of Shu and bring them all to the centre was read in the mountain stockades as the moment to act; at the same time the Emperor Wen was often ill in his later years and rumours of the dynasty's end were everywhere, which the insurgents in the mountains and in Lingnan alike believed. Outside pressure played a part as well: more than ten years after the fall of Chen, Chen loyalists and survivors had scattered into the mountains of the southwest, calling on the people to resist the government troops and defend the stockades, and urging the various strongholds to answer. Since the Liao revolts in Yizhou had already broken out several times in the Kaihuang era and each time been put down, the repeated calls on soldiers and equipment had worn the commandery troops down; and so when the rising came again in the first year of Renshou the prefectures and counties could no longer hold it themselves, and the court had to send an army into Shu.
impact: 此役的直接結果是蜀地秩序的短暫恢復，長遠影響則有三層。第一層是制度層：隋廷在平亂之後把「以夷制夷」寫進了新秩序——歸附首領授以官爵、仍舊牧其眾，新平之地設巡檢、置屯兵，郡縣編戶與羈縻首領並存的體制自此成形，這套辦法在唐代以羈縻州的形式固定下來，成為唐宋經營西南的基本框架。第二層是地理與軍事層：益州從此增置州縣與戍堡，劍閣道與岷江沿線的驛驛、倉儲加密，弩兵與常備郡兵的配額成為州縣的必要開支，蜀地由邊地變成編戶與羈縻交錯的內地，而這份治安成本從此長期落在蜀地百姓與州縣財政之上。第三層是隋朝自身的消耗：平亂所耗的兵糧與民役，在隋文帝晚年已使朝廷力不從心；他同年十一月崩，楊廣即位後，大業年間益州再爆大規模僚亂，隋廷以主力往討，國力大損，益州之亂遂與遼東、高句麗的戰事並列，成為隋朝速亡的幾大原因之一。
impactEn: The immediate result of this campaign was a brief restoration of order in Shu, but the long-term consequences ran on three levels. On the institutional level, after the suppression the Sui wrote the formula of using barbarians against barbarians into the new order: submitted leaders were granted official rank and left to rule their own people, the newly pacified ground was given patrol posts and garrison troops, and a system in which registered households and appointed barbarian chiefs coexisted was thereby formed; this approach was fixed in the Tang in the form of the jimi prefecture and became the basic framework by which the Tang and Song governed the southwest. On the geographical and military level, Yizhou gained further prefectures, counties and garrison forts, the relay stations and granaries along the Jianmen road and the Min river were multiplied, and the quota of crossbowmen and standing commandery troops became a necessary expense of every prefecture; Shu thus changed from a frontier region into an interior one in which registered households and jimi chiefs interlocked, and the cost of that security fell from then on for good upon the people of Shu and the finances of the prefectures. On the level of the dynasty's own strength, the soldiers, grain and labour spent on the suppression had already left the Sui unable to respond in the Emperor Wen's last years; he died in the eleventh month of the same year, and after Yang Guang came to the throne the Liao of Yizhou broke out in revolt on a large scale again in the Daye era, the court sending its main force to put it down at heavy cost, so the Yizhou revolt stands beside the wars against Liaodong and Goguryeo as one of the great reasons for the rapid collapse of the Sui.
result: 結果是隋朝平定了仁壽元年的益州僚亂：起事寨眾在圍困、斷糧與分化之下潰散，部分首領被誅，部分受招撫而降，其眾或散入深山，或被編為屯卒與民戶，州郡城得以重開，益州總管府恢復對山口的控制。史家對這一役的記載極略，斬獲人數、被俘人數、器械損耗與糧秣耗用皆無可考，所以能確定的只有一件事——隋廷沒有失去益州，平叛的代價由蜀地自己承擔。兵器層面同樣如此：秦弩這類守城器械在攻防兩端都起了作用，寨牆與山梁上的弩手封住了官軍的進攻節奏，攻方的弩手也掩護雲梯兵登寨，卻都沒有改變本役的結局；真正決定勝負的是山道與糧秣——只要蜀道可通、糧船能接續，攻方就耗得起；一旦後方接應不繼或雨季延長，圍軍會先於守軍耗盡。仁壽元年之後，隋文帝同年十一月崩，大業元年起局勢急轉，益州再亂；此役因此既是隋朝西南政策的收尾，也是隋末亂象的前奏。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Sui suppressed the Liao rising of the first year of Renshou in Yizhou: the insurgent strongholds fell apart under encirclement, the cutting of supplies and division; some leaders were killed, some surrendered on terms and were taken in, and their men either scattered into the deeper mountains or were enrolled as garrison soldiers and as registered households; the prefectural and county cities could be reopened, and the office of the Superintendent of Yizhou regained control of the passes. The historians record this campaign extremely briefly: the number killed, the number taken prisoner, the loss of equipment and the consumption of grain are all beyond recovery, so only one thing can be fixed, that the court did not lose Yizhou, and that the price of the suppression was paid by Shu itself. The same holds on the level of weapons. Crossbows such as the Qin crossbow played a part on both sides: the crossbowmen on the stockade walls and ridges held up the tempo of the government assault, and the government crossbowmen covered the ladder troops as they climbed, yet neither changed the outcome. What really decided it was the mountain roads and the grain: as long as the roads of Shu stayed open and the grain boats kept coming, the attacker could afford to wait; and once the support from the rear failed or the rainy season ran long, the besiegers were spent before the defenders were. After the first year of Renshou the Emperor Wen died in the eleventh month and the situation turned sharply with the first year of Daye, when Yizhou revolted again. This campaign is therefore both the closing move of Sui policy in the southwest and a prelude to the disorder of the dynasty's end.
